correctness.rationale: The displayed partial derivatives exclude projective singularities. For Y=mX+bZ with A=1+m³ nonzero, comparison of coefficients with A(X²+uX+v)² fixes u and v. For mb≠0 the linear coefficient gives D b³=8mA², D=m⁶+20m³−8, and the constant gives 9m²(4+m³)² b³=64A³; substitution yields H(m)=0 and is reversible on the stated roots. When b=0 and m≠0 there is a simple intersection at X=0 in the affine chart, while m=0 with b≠0 makes u=v=0 and cannot be a square. In the A=0 chart the intersection at infinity has odd multiplicity whether b vanishes or not. For X=cZ with c≠0 there is a simple intersection at infinity; X=0 and Z=0 give odd intersections too. This leaves the hyperflex Y=0 and the 27 listed lines. The two exact remainders for the finite triple locus vanish by sequential division by the monic cubic in m and then the d-equation over Q. The cubic discriminant is 432(27d⁹−1), nonzero at the indicated d. An independently coded field sweep uses the square test directly, finds 28 lines and reproduces all 324 doubles and 18 triples, including the nine specified affine ordinates. At any prime over 433 in a field containing all coefficients, the integral roots of the monic slope equation reduce bijectively (nine distinct roots), and the intercept cubes have unit denominator and three distinct roots for each slope; the same applies to the nine nonzero d-roots at this prime. Thus reduction is injective on lines and on all 18 exhibited points, and any concurrent line triple would map to one of the 18 known triples of lines. This proves exhaustiveness in characteristic zero, not just over the finite field. Transversality follows from distinct line directions at a point, and pair counting gives δ-total 378 and genus 351.
residual_risks: The positive-characteristic calculation is only a certificate at the specified prime, not a statement for other primes.

evidence: The general four-bitangent concurrence criterion implies a bielliptic involution. The Klein, Dyck and Komiya–Kuribayashi examples have distinct geometries; in particular the last has 324 double and 9 quadruple points.

originality.rationale: Credit the already known 28 bitangents, slope equation, automorphism-orbit profile, and the absence of quadruple or higher concurrence implied by the involution criterion for this odd-order automorphism group. The distinct claim is the exhaustive count and explicit two-locus description of triple points, and hence the complete incidence basket. No examined census or stronger theorem gives those triples for this quartic; the line equations are input for a new concurrency proof, not a published intersection table.
residual_risks: An older unindexed exact arrangement or underlying unpublished experimental census is possible. The accessible experimental description on large-group quartics does not say which triple counts were computed.

value.rationale: The singularity basket and explicit finite triple stratum classify all intersections of the complete canonical bitangent arrangement of a distinguished symmetric quartic. The number of triples, unlike the number of quadruples, is not determined by the known involution count; it is reusable data for comparisons of symmetric arrangements and local singularity calculations. The arithmetic genus is a consistency identity, not the main contribution.
residual_risks: A single canonical arrangement, not a full family classification.
